Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test `isUnixSymlinkIsFalseIfMoreThanOneFlagIsSet` expects that the method `isUnixSymlink()` should return false if more than one flag is set in the Unix mode of a Zip entry. The test case uses a real zip file entry "META-INF/maven/" and checks the `isUnixSymlink()` returns false.

Inspection of the `isUnixSymlink()` method shows that it returns true if and only if the bitwise AND of the Unix mode and `LINK_FLAG` equals `LINK_FLAG` itself, i.e., `(getUnixMode() & LINK_FLAG) == LINK_FLAG`. The `LINK_FLAG` is defined as `0120000` (octal) which represents the Unix symbolic link file type bit.

The `getUnixMode()` method returns the Unix mode bits for the entry, but notes that if the platform is not Unix, it returns 0. Otherwise, it isolates the top 16 bits of the external attributes by shifting and masking.

The bug described is that `isUnixSymlink()` returns true for entries with Unix permissions of `177777` (octal), which means more than just the link flag bit is set. The current implementation only checks that the `LINK_FLAG` bits are set but does not check if other bits are also set. Thus, if the mode is, for example, `177777`, the test `(mode & LINK_FLAG) == LINK_FLAG` will still be true because the `LINK_FLAG` bits are included in the mode, even though other bits are set. The method should also ensure that the mode corresponds exactly to a symbolic link type, without extraneous bits.

Hence, the root cause is that the `isUnixSymlink()` method's condition is insufficient. It only verifies that the link flag bit is set, allowing cases where other bits are simultaneously set, causing incorrect true return values for entries that are not pure symbolic links.

No evidence from recent unrelated bug reports affects this diagnosis.

The failing test confirms this problem, as it asserts false for an entry with "more than one flag" and it wrongly gets true with the current code.

Fixing `isUnixSymlink()` to more strictly check that the Unix mode equals exactly the `LINK_FLAG` bits (or matches an expected mode pattern for symlinks) will resolve the issue. Alternatively, the logic could mask out permission bits and focus only on the file type bits.

---

Methods involved: 
- `ZipArchiveEntry.isUnixSymlink()`
- `ZipArchiveEntry.getUnixMode()`
- Constants in `UnixStat` such as `LINK_FLAG` and possibly others to check file type bits properly.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
